cameraPolicy: Pin each renderer to the same resolved world-space camera for pixel comparisons. Record each engine's unmodified gameplay camera separately. The listed poses retain native camera1 gameplay anchors. The generated shared-probe camera, derived from the actual legacy reference quaternion including recoil and roll, is authoritative for controlled comparisons. Equal ticks do not establish cross-engine physical equivalence.
posePolicy: Controlled presentation probes must also share entity world/local poses, active entity set, animation time, particle event history/seed and lighting time wherever the renderer contract supports them. Save those exact probe inputs and their digests. A renderer-only probe adapter is permitted and must be labelled explicitly. Keep actual native gameplay/replay captures separate. Never substitute legacy simulation for a native gameplay result, import a cross-session snapshot, or hide misalignment by increasing error tolerances.

stages.acceptance: Original asset hashes and facility triangles are retained. Optic glass and extraction plane retain their actual alpha. Base-color, normal, metallic/roughness, emissive and sampler channels affect pixels. Compare source and adapted materials without admitting ignored fields.
Source ambient and authored lights, shadows, procedural sky, environment lighting and height fog affect pixels at the source values. Preserve unconfigured native rendering regressions.
Source HDR exposure, AgX, bloom, vignette and SMAA execute in the agreed order. Shader/LUT resources are included in installed exports.

Source fonts, widget tree and UI commands preserve text, layout, bars, hit/damage feedback and extraction banner. Decals, drone hover, muzzle/projectile/explosion prefabs, deterministic particles and camera/weapon poses remain visible at the transient probes.

Legacy, Qt and native browser captures use matching pose, resolution, seed and tick. Report whole-frame and named-region error, inspect paired images, and explain residuals. Select tolerances from measured references and controlled feature-removal failures. Do not declare parity from metadata or choose thresholds solely to pass the current renderer. Replay native combat/extraction after presentation changes.
